newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bargain-hunters limit falls in Jakarta stocks.
newsitem.headline: Bargain-hunters limit falls in Jakarta stocks.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed down in thin trading on Monday but ended off their lows, as players bargain-hunted big-caps near the close, brokers said.

The Jakarta composite index fell 0.79 points, or 0.12 percent, to close at 636.64 points after touching a day low of 633.28 points in the afternoon. Decliners led advancers by 84 to 37 with 71 issues unchanged.
Trading volume was small as the total turn-over was only around 302 billion rupiah compared with 340 billion rupiah on Friday.
"Bargain-hunting near the close helped limit the falls, but overall the tone remained weak as you can see that losers far outnumbered gainers," one broker said.
Big-caps Telkom, Indosat, Semen Gresik and Bimantara made modest rebounds due to the bargain-hunting, brokers said.
Brokers said reports of fresh riots in the central Javanese town of Pekalongan dampened the already weak market sentiment after a series of recent sharp falls.
A motor cycle dealership was looted and one person stabbed in fresh disturbances on Sunday near Pekalongan town in Indonesia's populous Central Java province, police and residents said.
Small stocks Mitra Rajasa, Surya Semesta, Suryamas and Bank Pikko were among the top four most actively traded due to speculation, brokers said.

The most actively traded stock, transportation firm Mitra Rajasa, fell 175 rupiah to 1,425 rupiah on profit-taking. Mitra made sharp gains recently after market talk that a business tycoon might buy a stake in the firm. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
